newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rumours started from abroad - Amnuay.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rumours started from abroad - Amnuay.

text.p: Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday that rumours this week that the Thai baht may be devalued and that he would resign were engineered by speculators from outside Thailand out to make money.

"Thailand is under threat. There is a group of people who spread all kinds of rumours to destabilise the economy and they make profit from it," he told reporters on his return to Thailand after attending a regional meeting in Tokyo.
The baht came under severe speculative attack this week on the devaluation rumours, prompting the Thai central bank to intervene heavily in the market to prop up the embattled currency.
Several other Asian central banks also intervened on behalf of the baht, dealers said.
The baht slump, especially on Wednesday, sent shockwaves through the stock exchange and forced it to close on Thursday at a near eight-year low.
Amnuay said he had heard since last Friday that there could be another speculative attack on the baht this week and had worked closely with the central bank to take necessary action if it happened.

On the plunging Thai stock market, Amnuay said there was a chance it could recover if negative rumours stopped circulating. The Thai stock index on Thursday closed down 2.35 percent at 557.87, its lowest since May 1989. The baht late on Thursday stabilised at 25.320/370 from a low of 26.330/430 late on Wednesday.
Amnuay reiterated that he believed his position as finance minister remained secure in the current government.
